These activities provided an opportunity for JUMP Into STEM participants to share their work with an industry partner and build connections. Collaboration with industry partners throughout the program helped make the JUMP Into STEM challenge more real and engaging for all participants. 4.2 Technology-to-Market Guidance Building science is a practical field where innovation is motivated by market needs. The technology-to-market requirement outlined in the project rules and rubric asked student participants to characterize the market in which their innovation might be deployed, develop a technology-to-market plan for potential deployment, and identify a key market adoption barrier. Because these market analysis ideas are often not part of building-science-related curricula, technology-to-market webinars and support documents were developed to provide some guidance. Strategies for a strong technology-to-market discussion include: • Clear identification of where the technology-to-market section is in the submission • Alignment of the discussion with the problem and solution • Indication of the scope of the market • Expression of the interconnectivity of stakeholders, cost-benefit analysis, and adoption barriers. Future implementations may benefit from additional discussion and examples, which can provide students with guidance while taking care to avoid causing bias that may lead to formulaic technology-to-market responses. 14 This report is available at no cost from the National Laboratory of the Rockies at www.nlr.gov/publications.
